key_insight: Current multimodal LLMs are not uniformly literate in scientific visualization: strong on some visual tasks, but notably weak on quantitative, texture-based, and integration-heavy SciVis understanding.
engineering_relevance: For scientific AI tools, benchmark design must include domain-specific visualization literacy, not just chart reading, to avoid overestimating real-world interpretive reliability.
method: Used a closed-world protocol on a standardized SciVis literacy test with 49 items across 18 visualizations/illustrations.
Compared model performance against 485 human participants across 8 techniques and 11 task types.
evidence_signal: The evaluation shows Gemini performed best overall, exceeding the human mean on the tested subsets, while open-source models stayed below the human baseline.
watch_item: Results come from a fixed benchmark and closed-world setup, so performance may not transfer to unseen visualization styles or broader scientific domains.
paper_title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy
